source: Curated from Congress.gov, Senate.gov, and National Archives historical records
note: Keyed by MM-DD. Dates without an entry fall back to the nearest notable fact of the month.

01-03.text: Shirley Chisholm is sworn in as the first Black woman in Congress. New Congresses have convened on January 3 since the 20th Amendment (1933).

01-10.text: A women's suffrage constitutional amendment is introduced in Congress for the first time, by Sen. Aaron Sargent of California.

01-23.text: The 24th Amendment is ratified, banning poll taxes in federal elections.

01-31.text: The House passes the 13th Amendment to abolish slavery, sending it to the states for ratification.

02-03.text: The 15th Amendment is ratified, barring racial discrimination in voting. On the same date in 1913, the 16th Amendment permitted the federal income tax.

02-10.text: The 25th Amendment is ratified, establishing presidential succession and disability procedures.

02-24.text: The House votes to impeach President Andrew Johnson — the first presidential impeachment in U.S. history.

02-25.text: Hiram Revels of Mississippi is sworn in as the first African American U.S. senator.

02-27.text: The 22nd Amendment is ratified, limiting presidents to two terms.

03-01.text: Congress's Yellowstone Act is signed, creating the world's first national park.

03-04.text: The First Congress under the Constitution convenes in New York City.

04-02.text: Jeannette Rankin of Montana is sworn in as the first woman in Congress — three years before nationwide women's suffrage.

04-04.text: The STOCK Act is signed, affirming that insider-trading laws apply to Congress and creating the rapid trade disclosures (PTRs) this site tracks.

04-08.text: The 17th Amendment is ratified, establishing direct popular election of U.S. senators.

05-07.text: The 27th Amendment is ratified — 202 years after James Madison proposed it — delaying congressional pay raises until after an election.

05-16.text: The Senate acquits President Andrew Johnson in his impeachment trial by a single vote.

06-02.text: The Indian Citizenship Act is signed, granting U.S. citizenship to Native Americans.

06-04.text: The Senate passes the 19th Amendment, sending women's suffrage to the states.

06-08.text: James Madison introduces the amendments that become the Bill of Rights.

06-10.text: The Equal Pay Act is signed, requiring equal pay for equal work regardless of sex.

06-22.text: The GI Bill is signed, funding education and home loans for millions of WWII veterans.

07-01.text: The 26th Amendment is ratified, lowering the voting age to 18 — the fastest ratification in history.

07-02.text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 is signed, outlawing segregation and employment discrimination.

07-04.text: The Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence. On the same date in 1966, the Freedom of Information Act — the foundation of U.S. government transparency — was signed.

07-09.text: The 14th Amendment is ratified, guaranteeing citizenship and equal protection under the law.

07-11.text: Congress establishes the United States Marine Corps as a permanent military force.

07-16.text: The Residence Act is signed, establishing Washington, D.C. as the permanent national capital.

07-26.text: The Americans with Disabilities Act is signed, the broadest civil-rights law for people with disabilities.

07-30.text: Medicare and Medicaid are created with the signing of the Social Security Amendments.

08-06.text: The Voting Rights Act is signed, banning discriminatory voting practices.

08-14.text: The Social Security Act is signed, creating the nation's retirement insurance system.

08-18.text: Tennessee's ratification makes the 19th Amendment — women's suffrage — part of the Constitution.

09-17.text: The U.S. Constitution is signed in Philadelphia — celebrated today as Constitution Day.

09-24.text: The Judiciary Act is signed, creating the federal court system and the Supreme Court's structure.

09-25.text: The First Congress sends 12 amendments — including the future Bill of Rights — to the states.

10-26.text: The Ethics in Government Act is signed, mandating public financial disclosure for officials after Watergate.

11-07.text: Jeannette Rankin becomes the first woman elected to Congress.

11-17.text: Congress meets for the first time in the unfinished U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

12-05.text: The 21st Amendment is ratified, repealing Prohibition — the only amendment ratified by state conventions.

12-06.text: The 13th Amendment is ratified, abolishing slavery.

12-15.text: The Bill of Rights is ratified — celebrated as Bill of Rights Day.
